summary: Fremont NF lookout above Summer Lake: a 72-foot Aermotor tower (dated 1931 or 1936) removed in 2003 after the 2002 fire; a rebuilt cabin rents since 2015.

facts.design: 72-foot all-steel Aermotor tower with a 7x7 steel cab
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 2003 after the 2002 Winter Rim fire weakened it; the ground cabin was rebuilt and reopened as a rental in 2015

staffing.status: lookouts recorded in 1944 and 1960; used in emergencies from the 1960s

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Fremont National Forest, now Fremont-Winema)

access.note: Fremont Point Cabin is rented through Recreation.gov. A privacy gate about a quarter mile past the day-use area opens with a reservation code. The tower is gone, so there is nothing to climb.

events.note: 72-foot Aermotor tower completed in September 1931, per the 1931 entry Forest Lookouts quotes; the register and firelookout.com date the steel tower to 1936
steel tower dated 1936 by the register, firelookout.com and Every Lookout in Oregon

condition survey: shutters damaged, cab paint peeling
one fire reported from the station in the fire season
safety inspection; the tower needs to be dismantled or restored
condition survey entry: abandoning in place
Winter Rim fire destroyed the ground cabin and greatly weakened the tower
steel tower removed due to structural weakening from the fire
registered May 20, 2011; nominated by Ray Kresek
foundation construction begun for the replacement cabin in September
replacement cabin completed in summer 2015 on the same footprint

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts quotes a 1931 entry saying the 72-foot tower was completed that September. The register, firelookout.com and Every Lookout in Oregon date the steel tower to 1936. The story reports both dates and keeps the 1931 entry as the only contemporary one.
Most sources give 72 feet (21.9 m). A 1942 ranger memo says 75 feet and a 1931 newspaper visit account says 80 feet. The record keeps 72 feet.
The Forest Service calls the cabin lost in 2002 the 1931 original. Forest Lookouts dates the living-quarters cabin to 1933. The record does not use the cabin date for the tower.

notes_for_editor: Brief record confirmed: Aermotor design (Forest Lookouts 1931 entry), 72 ft, status gone, FFLOS registration May 20, 2011. Build year (1931 vs 1936) and height (72, 75 or 80 ft) disagree and the story reports both. Access is public through Recreation.gov for the rebuilt cabin, not the tower. Photo credit to Howard Verschoor appears on firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts pages, but no image URLs were read, so no photos are recorded. The Herald and News article on the rebuild was not read because the site returned HTTP 429.
